answer: Each applicant plants one vine graft in a nursery row, its union painted in umber dye that fades in thirty days. Monthly the grower repaints the seal and photographs new shoots by a numbered tag, signed by a neighbor. Twice a season a warden rings the signal bell and checks seals against the registry. A bought graft fails, since its dye never fades and its shoots never lengthen. For 120 days the deposit is 150 tokens and the license 85 dollars, so 10,000 fake grafts freeze 1,500,000 tokens and cost 850,000 dollars. A graft is a fingerprint in living wood: it grows, and a copy stays still.
